transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I think the main reason I came in is just... I get pulled off track so easily. Like, I'll be trying to finish this dashboard I was supposed to be working on, and I'll get one Slack ping. Actually, my friend Emily just made a Slack channel for our dorm floor to organize a Secret Santa, which is kind of crazy to do in October, right? I love Christmas, but they're already playing holiday music at the mall and it's just way too early for that. I was trying to buy a sweater and I just couldn't even focus on the sizes. But, um, wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, getting off track. Yeah, so a Slack ping, or even just catching a song lyric in the background, or a totally random idea for another project pops into my head, and suddenly I've completely lost the thread of the dashboard I was supposed to be finishing.
Have you had these difficulties with attention and getting distracted since you were a child?

Yeah, pretty much. Like, even back in elementary school, my teachers were always writing comments on my report cards. They'd say I was rushing through my worksheets, or losing track of the directions, or talking over my classmates during group work. Actually, my second grade teacher, Mrs. Gable, she had this huge collection of those little troll dolls with the crazy hair? She kept them lined up on her desk, and I used to just stare at them during math. I always wanted the one with the bright pink hair, but she only gave them out as prizes if you got a perfect score on the spelling test. I was terrible at spelling, honestly. I always mixed up the "i before e" rule. But anyway, yeah, my parents actually had to sit right next to me while I did my homework back then, because otherwise I would just wander off to play with my dog or start drawing or something before I even finished half a page.
Do you often feel physically restless, like you have trouble sitting still or feel an inner urge to keep moving?

Oh, definitely. Like, if I have to sit still through a really long Zoom call or just quietly work in one place for too long, I start feeling this... I don't know, this uncomfortable pressure in my body? It's like I physically need to get up and pace, or at least do something with my hands. 

Which reminds me, I have this one Zoom class this semester, Intro to Sociology, and the professor literally talks in this complete monotone voice for an hour and a half. Last week, this girl in the class accidentally left her mic unmuted while she was ordering Starbucks at the drive-thru. She got an iced matcha latte with oat milk, which is actually my favorite drink, but I've been trying to make them at home recently to save money. Matcha powder is so expensive, though! I bought this one brand off Amazon and it tasted like literal dirt. You really have to get the ceremonial grade if you want it to taste good. 

But um... wait, yeah, so sitting still. I just get that weird pressure where I have to keep moving my hands or I just feel like I'm going to crawl out of my skin.
